projects.name: Enterprise MCP Platform
projects.description: A platform concept for securely exposing enterprise APIs and capabilities to AI agents through MCP.

caseStudy.problem: AI agents need access to enterprise capabilities, but exposing APIs directly creates security, access-control and governance risk.
caseStudy.product: A platform that abstracts enterprise APIs and capabilities behind MCP, so AI agents can be enabled safely and consistently.
caseStudy.architecture: Enterprise APIs are exposed through an MCP platform with security, access control and data governance, then consumed by AI agents.
caseStudy.decisions: MCP as the standard interface; API abstraction; access control and governance as platform capabilities; enabling agents without direct API exposure.
caseStudy.challenges: Securing agent access, governing data, and keeping integrations consistent across the enterprise.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Security rigor versus agent flexibility; abstraction versus integration fidelity.

projects.name: AI Software Factory
projects.category: AI Product Engineering · Agentic Software Development
projects.description: An AI-driven software development orchestration platform designed to transform product requirements into implementation-ready software changes.

caseStudy.problem: Bridging the gap between product requirements and high-quality implementation changes — reducing the friction, inconsistency and review overhead that slow down AI-assisted development.
caseStudy.product: An orchestration platform that turns a business requirement into a specification, plans the work, dispatches specialist AI agents, and produces an implementation-ready change through review and pull requests.
caseStudy.architecture: A pipeline of stages — requirement intake, specification, planning, agent dispatch, implementation, testing/review and pull request — coordinated by agent orchestration, with context engineering and git-based workflows.
caseStudy.decisions: Specification as the source of truth; specialist agents over a single monolithic agent; automated review gates; git and pull requests as the collaboration interface.
caseStudy.challenges: Keeping generated changes consistent, giving each agent the right context, and maintaining quality through automated review.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Balancing agent autonomy against review rigor, context size against relevance, and generation speed against correctness.

projects.name: SpecKitBasic
projects.description: A lightweight approach to using specifications as the single source of truth for AI-assisted software development.
projects.tagline: A lightweight approach to bringing structure and context to AI-assisted software development.

caseStudy.problem: AI-assisted development becomes unpredictable without a clear, structured source of truth for what should be built.
caseStudy.product: A lean workflow where a requirement becomes a specification, drives an architecture/plan, and guides implementation and validation.
caseStudy.architecture: A minimal pipeline from requirement to specification to plan to implementation to validation, focused on structured context rather than heavy tooling.
caseStudy.decisions: Specification as the source of truth; lightweight rules; structured requirements; prioritizing consistency over breadth of automation.
caseStudy.challenges: Managing context efficiently and keeping requirements structured enough for reliable AI-assisted development.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Simplicity versus capability; structure versus speed of iteration.

projects.name: MARK1 — AI Technical Support Agent
projects.description: An AI agent designed to investigate technical support requests using enterprise documentation, support tickets and legacy source code.

caseStudy.problem: Technical support in enterprise software requires investigating scattered documentation, historical tickets and legacy code — a slow, knowledge-intensive process.
caseStudy.product: An agent that investigates a support request end to end, combining retrieval across documentation, tickets and codebase with dependency analysis to produce a grounded technical answer.
caseStudy.architecture: An agent orchestrator built with LangGraph coordinates hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector search) over documentation, tickets and code, performs dependency analysis, and produces a grounded LLM response — with evaluation and observability.
caseStudy.decisions: Agent orchestration via LangGraph; hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector) over a single LLM call; dependency analysis to understand code relationships; grounding answers in retrieved evidence.
caseStudy.challenges: Retrieval quality across heterogeneous sources, grounding to avoid hallucination, and understanding legacy code dependencies.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: Retrieval latency versus answer quality; hybrid search coverage versus index complexity; agent autonomy versus control.

projects.name: Luna — Enterprise AI Knowledge Platform
projects.description: A multi-tenant AI platform designed to transform organizational knowledge into context-aware AI capabilities.
projects.tagline: Product architecture / platform concept / ongoing development

caseStudy.problem: Organizational knowledge is fragmented across documents, meetings, incidents, APIs and integrations, and cannot be turned into reliable AI capabilities at enterprise scale.
caseStudy.product: A multi-tenant platform that consolidates organizational knowledge into a knowledge layer, grounds it with RAG, exposes it through AI agents, and delivers it to business applications.
caseStudy.architecture: Multiple ingestion sources feed a knowledge layer with Qdrant-based retrieval and LangGraph agents, governed by multi-tenancy, observability, governance and privacy-by-design (LGPD), and exposed through integrations to business applications.
caseStudy.decisions: Multi-tenancy as a first-class concern; a knowledge layer abstraction; RAG for grounded retrieval; governance and privacy-by-design (LGPD) from the start.
caseStudy.challenges: Isolating tenants, governing data, and balancing retrieval quality with governance and privacy requirements.
caseStudy.tradeoffs: RAG fidelity versus complexity; governance overhead versus speed; multi-tenant isolation versus operational cost.
